title: Lab to Field
notes: Introduce the project in one line: plant-disease AI gets about 99% on lab photos but fails on real farm photos. We measured that failure honestly, fixed part of it, and made the model say 'not sure' when it doesn't know.

title: Models that ace the lab fail in the field
notes: Published: Mohanty 2016, 99.35% to 31.4% on web images; Xiang 2026, ResNet-50 99.73% to 32.05% while still ~80% confident. Left three columns are lab photos, right three are field photos of the same disease.

title: Our approach: one step per course module
notes: Each notebook covers one step: 01 problem and data, 02 CNN from scratch, 03 transfer learning, 04 augmentation, 05 training choices, 06 explain and export. The test set is the final exam, never used to choose anything.

title: Making the test honest before training anything
notes: Two leaks fixed: same-leaf photos across splits, and duplicate web images. The corner test used a random forest on four 8x8 corner patches only; chance is 3.6%.

title: CNN from scratch: 95.8% in the lab, 8.9% in the field
notes: Conv parameters = k·k·Cin·Cout, BatchNorm = 2·C, Linear = in·out + out. ReLU, pooling and dropout have none. The red flag is the confidence: 78% while being right 9% of the time.

title: Pretrained features help; real field photos help most
notes: Linear probe trains only the last layer; fine-tuning trains everything with a small learning rate. Our ResNet-50 (32.2%) and DINOv2 (46.2%) match published numbers (32.05% and ~41-43%). MobileNetV3 is deployed because it is phone-sized: 5.5M parameters, depthwise separable convolutions.

title: Targeted augmentation beats generic augmentation
notes: On field validation bg_field narrowly won (28.9 vs 27.7) while bg_synthetic was better on test (39.0 vs 31.4). We followed validation anyway; the disagreement shows how noisy small field sets are.

title: Training choices: label smoothing makes the model honest
notes: AdamW and SGD are within noise; AdamW kept. Focal loss did not help because classes were already capped at 500 photos. The reliability diagram compares confidence with accuracy; the diagonal is perfect calibration.

title: Final model: 64% in the field, and it knows when it's unsure
notes: Grad-CAM shows where the model looked: middle row is the lab-only model, bottom row the final model. The final model gets 4 of 5 right and looks at lesions more often, but sometimes still at background. The collage image gets 11% confidence, so the app would say not sure.

title: From notebook to app
notes: The app never needs PyTorch for prediction. Abstain threshold 0.54 and temperature were set on validation data. INT8 would need quantization-aware training (Module 7).

title: What we learned
notes: End with the three lessons and the next steps for Group Project 2. Then take questions.
